title: Hamilton Beach One Press Programmable Dispensing 12 Cup Coffee Maker with Internal Coffee Pot, Stays Warm and Fresh for Hours, 60 oz. Removable Reservoir, Black & Stainless Steel (47950)

reviews.title: Great coffee maker!
reviews.body: I love this coffee maker. I had a much older (5+ years) Hamilton Beach model of this style but without the program, brew settings, etc. which still worked just fine when I bought this one. The water reservoir in that one was accessible only from the top, behind the basket. I saw this one in Target but decided not to buy it until I read reviews. The Amazon price was the same as Target but the reviews helped me make my decision easy. I love that the reservoir can be detached. The numbers on it are easy to see in case you forget how much water you poured in. There are also numbers on the other side so you can see how much brewed coffee is left. The program options are awesome - bold, regular, and 1-4 cup settings. I love that you can also brew iced coffee, which turns out perfectly without tasting diluted. That was actually the main thing that attracted my eye to this model. The start time can also be programmed as can the "keep warm" time (1-4 hrs). I was already a fan of the dispensing mechanism from years of using my older model. Compared to a separate carafe, this way just makes sense for keeping the coffee hot without that burned taste you get from the pot sitting on the burner too long.The cons: it's somewhat cheaply made. The reservoir doesn't have a great fit against the main body of the system. There is a gap between them that feels like it could be better. The lid also has room for improvement of fit. The drip tray doesn't fit in as snugly as my older model's. When I moved the unit back and forth across the counter the tray would sometimes come off easily. I bent the plastic "latch" a little so it would hug the notch a bit better so it's not really a big problem. It would be a better design if the tray snapped into the main body of the machine. Note: the drip tray is in two pieces and both can be removed for easy cleaning. The last con is that it tends to be noisier than my older model - sort of a hissing noise. It doesn't bother me but it is noticeable.Even with the cons I'd still recommend it.

reviews.title: Great brew station but fatal flaws
reviews.body: The Hamilton Beach Brew Station is my all-time favorite coffee machine. We have purchased four of them to date after trying a cuisine art unit that routinely leaked all over the counter.  None of the four Hamilton Beach units ever leaked. The controls are easy to use, and the unit makes exactly the coffee we enjoy. We do occasionally clean the metal filter at the bottom of the Coffee Tank by pouring some “clean that pot” liquid and following the instructions – does a nice job. We also use filtered water along with both a metal filter and a paper filter in the Filter Basket for very consistent taste. Excellent job Hamilton Beach.Hamilton Beach Engineers get your act together: Unfortunately, there is a flaw in the design that causes unimaginable frustration and very limited product life of maybe a year. The flaw ruined the first three Brew Stations that we bought. We discovered that the Coffee Dispenser Bar would no longer release coffee from the Coffee Tank (see A in Frame 1 of the figure).  Pushing that Bar should force the plastic Lever B (in Frame 2) toward the front of the unit.  One can see, by tipping the Coffee Tank backward, the plastic Coffee Release Valve C (in Frame 3); the valve has a very stiff spring to prevent coffee from accidently dripping out. At first, it seems the lever B fails by no longer making contact with the valve but placing a pad between B and C does not help and eventually Lever B breaks away. We found that Lever B is quite flexible in a failed unit compared with a new unit. This means Lever B in a failed unit does not have the rigidity to open the Valve C to release the coffee.  Moral of the Story: Hamilton Beach, please consider making the Lever B and associated components out of metal. A couple of events might be occurring (or both). First repeated pressure on the Lever B might fatigue the plastic. Second, the Lever B is next to the high temperature heating element and high temperature is well known to deteriorate the strength of plastic.  After all these years, this defect cannot be a surprise to the company. Perhaps replacement parts are available. We only finally figured out the problem when we were in a position to compare failed and new units.Finally, we plan on returning the new unit that arrived today because the Lid hinge was apparently damaged during shipping – the plastic protrusion forming a hinge was broken off – the Lid flaps around.But again, we absolutely love the Hamilton Beach Brew Station but definitely not the nasty flaws.Update:  Engineering and quality control departments need massive downsizing:  The new Brew Station leaked all over the counter.  First one with this flaw out of the 5 we tried. Surprising the Hamilton Beach lawyers don't start to worry.

reviews.title: Pretty good machine with a couple of minor design flaws
reviews.body: This Coffee maker has a lot of good features.First and foremost - it brews good coffee.  It keeps coffee warm without overcooking it so you don't get an overly bitter beverage like you do with carafes sitting on hot plates for long periods of time.Initial setup and cleaning were pretty easy.  I like that the unit is so modular.  Taking the water reservoir, filling it and reinstalling it on the unit is a less messy process than holding a pitcher high over a coffee maker to fill it, and means I'm not constantly reserving a pitcher for that process.Overall, i really like this coffee maker after several days of use.There are several negatives, all minor annoyances that I think could be addressed in future models.  Keep in mind that despite the amount of detail, these are MINOR issues to me.  I'm living with them.1.  The LED is SO BRIGHT.  When you've programmed coffee for the next morning, you better not plan to sleep within s sight line of this thing.  It's like a light house.  Minor plus, I no longer turn on a light if I got to get a glass of water at midnight.  The LED lights my way.2.  The coffee maker slides away from you when dispensing.  Pushing your coffee cup against the lever to release the coffee is an act of very fine motor control; not something that exists before I've had my coffee.  So, despite my best efforts, the coffee maker runs away from the cup until I've got it backed against the wall.  Then it gives me coffee.  I might put some sticky pads on its feet in the next week or so before my wife has a bad morning and I have to get a new coffee maker.3.  The coffee level in the holding tank is hard to read.  You're just looking at the coffee level in an opaque gauge; no little floating ball or anything.  So what happens after you brew a batch is that everything above the 'coffee mark' fogs up.  So then your wife comes along with her tanker cup and fills it, dropping the level by about 4 cups worth or so.  The coffee level drops, but it doesn't look so much like it did because the 'fog line' looks like the 'coffee line'.  Then you come along thinking there's like 4 more cups of coffee, shove your cup against the lever and - nada.  One full cup of disappointment to start out your day.  Welcome to America.At the end of the day, the good features outweigh the negatives by quite a bit for this unit and I'm pretty happy with it.

reviews.title: I am so glad i found this product on Amazon!
reviews.body: When we moved into our new home, our coffee maker didn’t make it. I quickly realized how hard it is to find a carafe-free coffee maker, so I grabbed a standard (brand name) coffee maker off the shelf at Costco. Big mistake. I quickly realized I really don’t like having a carafe, and on top of that, the machine was awkward and frustrating to use. Within days, I was determined to return it.I went on Amazon and, after some searching, I luckily found the exact carafe-free coffee maker I had purchased back in 2022—the one that broke during the move. I ordered it immediately and couldn’t wait for it to arrive.As soon as it was delivered, I set it up in my new coffee bar and instantly smiled. It fit perfectly, looked so much better, and felt right. One feature I especially love is the removable water reservoir—I don’t have to lug water across the kitchen to the coffee bar or drag the entire coffee maker to the sink just to fill it.Setup was refreshingly easy. Setting the time, brew schedule, and preferences was so intuitive that I didn’t need the manual—or a PhD—to figure it out.The very next morning, the coffee brewed right on time, and both my husband and I commented that it even tasted better than the coffee from the machine now sitting on the counter waiting to be returned.I honestly couldn’t be happier with this purchase. If you’re on the fence about buying a carafe-free coffee maker, take the leap—you won’t regret it.Quick highlights:--Carafe-free (no messy pouring or cleanup)--Removable water reservoir (no lifting or hauling)--Extremely easy setup and programming--Great-looking and compact on the counter--Consistently great-tasting coffee

reviews.title: Good product ... bad timing!
reviews.body: Pros: The coffee maker makes great coffee. It takes about 10 minutes for a pot to be completed. Love the one cup feature instead of a carafe!!! No spilling or dripping on the counter.Cons: Makes a bubbling noise while it keeps coffee warm.Tried to use the program the first night...forgot to turn on the program...my error. I tried the next night. Woke up at 6:15, coffee should be ready because it is programmed for 6AM. I walked in and it read 5:43 AM. I went back to the bedroom and looked at my clock and my phone both said 6:18. So I thought I messed up putting in the time. I set it again the next night...again it didnt go off and was 30 min behind again. If I dont set it the program the time stays. Thus so far is the biggest downside to the coffee pot.It is a little cumbersome to clean the holding station. Not a show stopper though.Would like to return it for a new one due to the program timer issue, but since I have used it multiple days and thrown away the box not sure I can. I would BTW get the same pot.

reviews.title: Hamilton Beach Coffee Maker
reviews.body: I love this coffee maker!  This is my 5th or 6th of the same coffee maker.  I've tried others in between - some are nice, however, with arthritis, this is so much easier on my hands!  I don't have to lift the entire pot.  With this one, all I have to lift is my cup!  I get it ready the night before and when I wake up the next day, I have fresh, hot coffee waiting for me!  If I use it during the day, it's fast, I can sneak a cup before it finishes brewing.  I set the timer for how many hours I want it to stay hot and it turns off automatically.  I can't say enough good things about this coffee maker.

features: FRESH FLAVOR LONGER WITHOUT THE CARAFE: This coffee maker replaces the carafe with quick and easy dispensing of fresh, flavorful coffee anytime. Without a carafe, there's no breaking, spilling, or cleaning baked-on coffee stains.Filter type:Reusable
NO MORE SCORCHED OR BURNED COFFEE: The Hamilton Beach coffee maker's internal warming heater keeps coffee warm and fresh for hours. It works without a carafe, so coffee won't burn or scorch.

HOT COFFEE WHEN YOU'RE READY ONE FRESH CUP AT A TIME: The 12 cup coffee maker dispenses hot coffee directly into a cup or a 7" travel mug whenever you're ready for a cup by simply pressing the dispensing bar.

EASY TO FILL WITH REMOVABLE WATER RESERVOIR: The water reservoir removes for easy filling and cleaning. With a 12 cup capacity, you can brew enough coffee for everyone at once. Enclosed brewing system with internal heater keeps coffee hot and fresh for up to 4 hours
KNOW WHEN IT'S TIME TO CLEAN: Helpful reminders on the digital display let you know when it's time to clean the coffee maker, so you never forget.
